Student Reviews Overview — Research on All Universities, in One Place

In Oct 2026, we researched student feedback and last-year placements for 13 of the universities on this site across Reddit, Instagram, YouTube, podcasts, comments and review platforms. LPU Online was added to this site after that research, so its page carries no researched findings yet — and no invented review has been added for it. Below is the cross-university overview from that research — in FRC's own words, with a label attached to every point. The full detail for each university (praise, complaints, placements) is on its own page. There is no ranking, no star rating and no score here.

Evidence thin — no firm ranking Do not rank these universities on criticism. Review volumes vary, the sources mix campus and online students, and social search mostly surfaced promotional material. That is why only themes are given below — there is no ‘worst university’ list.

The Most Repeated Theme — Placement Expectations vs Reality

The most repeated complaint theme across all online offerings is this: students who expected campus-style placement drives instead received assistance / portals. This pattern appeared for NMIMS CDOE, Amity Online, MUJ Online, CU Online, DPU-COL and Jamia Online — in secondary guides or individual reviews for every one of them.

The Second Big Theme — Admin / Support Delays

  • Amity Online: tickets being marked closed without resolution, transcript / marksheet delays, and a CGPA threshold reportedly being raised near graduation Reported claim — not verified policy
  • CU Online: a 2024 review reported unanswered counsellor calls and LMS issues.
  • MUJ Online: 2024 reviews reported app slowness, deadline changes and unanswered chats.
  • UPES Online: a single 2023 review reported doubt emails going unanswered.

Two Watch-Outs — Both With Their Labels

  • Campus — NOT online Mizoram University — placement depth: multiple independent campus reviews from 2017, 2018, 2023, 2025 and 2026 republications agree on few / no campus drives, dependence on pool-campus drives and low placement volumes, and the verified NIRF figures are also the lowest in this set (132 placed in total in 2023-24). This is campus / affiliated-college evidence, not evidence about MZU Online. Evidence thin — verify with recent online learners
  • Online-only UPES Online — online support / placement: a verified Shiksha review (6 Feb 2023) alleges no placements for online MBA students, rare lectures, inadequate material and unanswered doubts. This is the harshest single piece of online-specific testimony in this research, but Single review (n=1) — do not generalise — it cannot outweigh Mizoram's repeated pattern on volume, and fresh verification is needed before any stronger claim.

The Remaining Patterns — At a Glance

  • Campus — NOT online Amity Jaipur the placement-specific campus evidence is the most consistently negative — multiple Shiksha / Zollege reviews (Feb 2025, Sep 2025) report a low placed share, few visiting companies and reliance on self-placement. This is about the Jaipur campus; do not transfer it to Amity Online.
  • JAIN has the widest spread of complaint types (campus + online combined) — placement shortfalls in some courses, slide-based teaching, overcrowding, high fees, and one serious third-party-agent online complaint (Dec 2021). That agent complaint is Single, old account — not a verified current pattern.
  • SMU's criticism is the most mode-split — campus engineering complaints alongside separate, sharp distance-mode complaints (centre facilities, reports of placement support not being available). It is the most heterogeneous — not necessarily the largest by volume.
  • Campus — NOT online MAHE Manipal's criticism is the most consistent but narrow — cost + strict hostel rules + academic pressure, alongside praise for infrastructure and recruiter breadth.
  • The thinnest criticism bases: AMU Online and Shoolini Online (online-specific). AMU's criticism is mild (‘average’ placement volume / salary) and small in number; Shoolini Online's criticism is generic (networking, perceived value) and mostly campus-based — its most extreme review is unverified and was not used in any conclusion.

Placements — The Full Picture

No university in this set publishes a verified, online-only, year-labelled placed-student count that can be compared like-for-like — apart from two flagged exceptions: Amity Online's 1,000 (2025) Secondary source, citing official data — not directly verified and MUJ Online MBA's 56 Year unclear — do not label as confirmed 2025. Every other usable placed number is whole-university NIRF data, given on each university's own page with the programme length and year and clearly labelled ‘NOT online-only’. The one line from this research that a senior can honestly stand behind is this: online placements depend on placement assistance and your own effort — they are not a guaranteed outcome like a campus drive.

Social-Source Warning

Promotional — not independent The Instagram / YouTube / podcast material found in this sweep was heavily promotional or testimonial-style (especially for CU Online, Shoolini Online and DPU-COL, Sep–Oct 2026), and for many online programmes social search produced almost no usable independent criticism. That is a missing source, not proof of satisfaction. For Jamia, Mizoram Online, AMU Online, UPES Online and Shoolini Online, online-specific criticism from Reddit / YouTube / podcasts was thin in usable form.

How Your Programme Is Structured — Semester by Semester

Most two-year postgraduate programmes on this site run across 4 semesters, and the three-year undergraduate programmes across 6. This is the pattern the brochures follow — the exact subjects for your university are listed semester by semester on its course page.

1

Semesters 1–2

Core Foundations

The core subjects of your field — for an MBA, subjects like Marketing Management, Financial Accounting, Organizational Behavior and Business Analytics; for BCA/MCA, programming and computing fundamentals; for commerce degrees, accounting and finance basics. Continuous assessment and assignments run alongside.

2

Semester 3

Specialization Begins

You move into your chosen specialization with elective subjects — and, in programmes like CU Online's MBA and Amity's healthcare MBA, a minor or capstone project starts here, based on your specialization.

3

Semester 4

Advanced Electives & Final Project

Advanced specialization electives plus the final project — NMIMS, for example, carries a 6-credit project in Semester 4, while CU Online closes with Capstone Project – II. This is where your degree work comes together.

4

After Completion

Degree & Career

On completing all semesters and assessments, the university awards the degree. Programmes here total 90–102 credits at PG level (for example, 90 at MUJ and 102 at NMIMS) — the exact credit structure is on each course page.

Eligibility & How to Apply

The general rules below cover most programmes on this site. The exact eligibility, marks and documents for your course are on its course page — and our counsellor confirms them for you before you apply.

Eligibility at a Glance

Undergraduate programmes (BBA, BCA, B.Com, BA)

Pass in 10+2 from a recognized board. Students due to appear in their 10+2 examination can also apply where the brochure allows it (for example, JAIN Online).

Postgraduate programmes (MBA, MCA, M.Com, MA)

A bachelor's degree from a recognized university. Most MBA brochures here ask for 50% aggregate marks (45% for reserved categories); Amity's healthcare MBA accepts 40%, with a test option below that.

ABC ID & DEB ID

Some universities (Chandigarh University Online and NMIMS, as per their brochures) require an Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) ID and a UGC-DEB ID on the application form. Our counsellor will walk you through creating both — free.

How to Apply — 5 Steps

  • Step 1 — Choose your university, course and specialization using the finder and course pages above.
  • Step 2 — Check the eligibility and keep your documents ready (see our documents checklist).
  • Step 3 — Fill the enquiry form below — your details open in WhatsApp, ready to send to +91 72360 32906.
  • Step 4 — Apply on the university's official portal and upload your documents for verification.
  • Step 5 — Pay the fee through the university's official process — on approval you receive your enrolment and LMS login, and classes begin online.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is this the official website of these universities?
No. FindRightCollege is an independent admission-guidance service. We show course information from the universities' brochures and help you with admission. Final admission and fee payment always happen through the university's official process.
What happens after I fill the form?
As soon as you submit, WhatsApp opens with your filled details ready. Press Send and they reach our number +91 72360 32906. The FRC team will then call you and explain the next steps.
Are online degrees valid?
The online programmes on this page are described as UGC-entitled in the universities' brochures. Even so, before taking admission, please also verify the UGC entitlement and accreditation (NAAC grade) yourself on the university's official website — that is why we give these details on every course page.
Is anything hidden in the fees?
We have listed every fee given in the brochures — semester fee, application fee, registration and exam fee wherever they apply — separately on each course page. Where a brochure figure was ambiguous, we have added a note asking you to verify it on the official site.
Why is the city asked "as per Aadhaar card"?
Your city in the admission documents should match your Aadhaar card, so please write the same city that is on your Aadhaar card. Please note — we ask only for the city. We never ask for your Aadhaar number.
Can I do these courses along with a job?
All of these programmes are in 100% online mode, so they are designed for working professionals and students who need flexibility. The exact class and exam schedule differs by university — we will confirm it for your course when you enquire.
Which courses can I apply for here?
All 142 online programmes listed on this site, from 17 universities — UG: BBA, BCA, B.Com, BA, BA-JMC and B.Sc (Hons) IT. PG: MBA (including Executive MBA and MBA for Working Professionals), MCA, M.Com, MA, MA-JMC, MSc and Master of Social Work. Plus other programmes: PG certificate (PGCP), PGP, diploma and certificate programmes. Pick your university and course in the form above and we will guide you.
How to do an online MBA — how do I do an MBA online?
Choose a UGC-entitled university, check that you meet the eligibility (a bachelor's degree, usually with 50% marks), fill the admission form, upload your documents, pay the fee and complete the university's verification — after that you get your enrolment and LMS login and classes begin online. The full step-by-step process is in our Online MBA admission guide.
Is an online MBA valid in India?
An online degree from a UGC-entitled university is treated at par with a regular degree for jobs and further study, as per UGC rules. Always verify the university's UGC entitlement on its official website or the UGC-DEB portal before paying any fee. Read our guide on UGC approved online degrees.
Can I get admission without an entrance exam?
Most online programmes on this page take direct admission based on your qualifying-exam marks — no CAT or other entrance test is mentioned in their brochures. Each university's exact rule is on its course page, and our counsellor confirms it for your course when you enquire.
Which documents are required for online degree admission?
Generally: 10th and 12th mark sheets and certificates, graduation mark sheets and degree for PG courses, a government photo ID, passport-size photographs and your signature. The exact list differs by university — see the full list in our documents required guide.
